ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is the interface circuit of the 8085A and a 3-to-8 line decoder. The high-order address bus bits A15, A14, and A13 are respectively connected to the three select inputs of the decoder; the output terminals on the right side of the decoder are numbered from 0 to 7, among which output terminal 2 is used to gate the output port/peripheral path. The decoder also has enable terminals E1, \bar{E}_2, and \bar{E}_3; in the figure, E1 is generated by A12 and A11 with an inversion condition through a gate circuit, and IO/M and WR are connected as control signals to enable-related lines. Reasoning: According to the specified method, decoder output 2 is selected, so the select inputs I2 I1 I0 = 010, corresponding to A15 A14 A13 = 010. E1 is active high, and the gate circuit in the figure requires A12 = 1 and A11 = 0. IO/M and WR are only used as control enable signals, not as address bits. If the remaining undecoded low-order address bits are taken as 0, then the address bit pattern is A15...A0 = 0101 0000 0000 0000₂, namely 5000H.
